text:
Let $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ be two relations defined on $\mathrm{ℝ}$ by

$aR_{1}b⇔ab\geq 0$ and $aR_{2}b⇔a\geq b$

Then,
options: $R_{1}$ is an equivalence relation but not $R_{2}$
$R_{2}$ is an equivalence relation but not $R_{1}$
neither $R_{1}$ nor $R_{2}$ is an equivalence relation
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$aR_{1}b⇔ab\geq 0$

So, definitely $(a,a)\in R_{1}$ as $a^{2}\geq 0$

If $(a,b)\in R_{1}\Rightarrow (b,a)\in R_{1}$

But if $(a,b)\in R_{1},(b,c)\in R_{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ Then $(a,c)$ may or may not belong to $R_{1}$

{Consider $a=-5,b=0,c=5$ so $(a,b)$ and $(b,c)\in R_{1}$ but $ac<0$}

So, $R_{1}$ is not equivalence relation

$aR_{2}b⇔a\geq b$

$(a,a)\in R_{2}\Rightarrow$ so reflexive relation

If $(a,b)\in R_{2}$ then $(b,a)$ may or may not belong to $R_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ So not symmetric

Hence it is not equivalence relation

text: The area of the smaller region enclosed by the curves $y^{2}=8x+4$ and  $x^{2}+y^{2}+4\sqrt{3}x-4=0$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Circle: $(x+2\sqrt{3})^{2}+y^{2}=16$, centre $C(-2\sqrt{3},0)$, radius 4. Parabola: $y^{2}=8\left (x+\dfrac{1}{2}\right )$, vertex $V\left (-\dfrac{1}{2},0\right )$.

Substituting $y^{2}=8x+4$ in the circle gives $x^{2}+(8+4\sqrt{3})x=0$, so $x=0$ (the other root is less than $-\dfrac{1}{2}$, where the parabola does not exist). The curves meet at $(0,2)$ and $(0,-2)$.

The smaller region lies inside both curves: the parabola bounds it on the left (through $V$) and the arc of the circle on the right.


[IMG]

Part left of the $y$-axis, between the arms of the parabola for $-\dfrac{1}{2}\leq x\leq 0$:

$\int\limits _{-1/2}^{0}2\sqrt{8x+4}dx=\left [\dfrac{(8x+4)^{3/2}}{6}\right ]_{-1/2}^{0}=\dfrac{8}{6}=\dfrac{4}{3}$

Part right of the $y$-axis is the circular segment cut off by the chord $x=0$. The chord is at distance $2\sqrt{3}$ from $C$, so $\cos θ=\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{4}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $θ=30^{\circ }$, and the chord subtends $60^{\circ }=\dfrac{π}{3}$ at $C$:

$\text{segment}=\text{sector}-\text{triangle}=\dfrac{1}{2}(4^{2})\dfrac{π}{3}-\dfrac{1}{2}\times 4\times 2\sqrt{3}=\dfrac{8π}{3}-4\sqrt{3}$

Total area:

$\dfrac{4}{3}+\dfrac{8π}{3}-4\sqrt{3}=\dfrac{1}{3}\left (4-12\sqrt{3}+8π\right )$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: Let $y=y_{1}(x)$ and $y=y_{2}(x)$ be two distinct solutions of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}=x+y$, with $y_{1}(0)=0$ and $y_{2}(0)=1$ respectively. Then, the number of points of intersection of $y=y_{1}(x)$ and $y=y_{2}(x)$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=x+y$

Let $x+y=t$

$1+\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dt}{dx}$

$\frac{dt}{dx}-1=t\Rightarrow \int \frac{dt}{t+1}=\int dx$

$\ln |t+1|=x+C^{'}$

$|t+1|=Ce^{x}$

$|x+y+1|=Ce^{x}$

For $y_{1}(x),y_{1}(0)=0\Rightarrow C=1$

For $y_{2}(x),y_{2}(0)=1\Rightarrow C=2$

$y_{1}(x)$ is given by $|x+y+1|=e^{x}$

$y_{2}(x)$ is given by $|x+y+1|=2e^{x}$

At point of intersection

$e^{x}=2e^{x}$

No solution

So, there is no point of intersection of $y_{1}(x)$ and $y_{2}(x)$.

text: Let $⃗{a}=α\hat{i}+\hat{j}+β\hat{k}$ and $⃗{b}=3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ be two vectors, such that $⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}=-\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$. Then the projection of $⃗{b}-2⃗{a}$ on $⃗{b}+⃗{a}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{a}=α\hat{i}+\hat{j}+β\widehat{k}$, $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}$

$\vec{a}\times \vec{b}=-\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+12\widehat{k}$

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ α & 1 & β \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \end{array}\right |=-\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+12\widehat{k}$

$4+5β=-1\Rightarrow β=-1$

$-5α-3=12\Rightarrow α=-3$

$\vec{b}-2\vec{a}=3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}-2\left (-3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\widehat{k}\right )$

$\vec{b}-2\vec{a}=9\hat{i}-7\hat{j}+6\widehat{k}$

$\vec{b}+\vec{a}=\left (3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}\right )+\left (-3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\widehat{k}\right )$

$\vec{b}+\vec{a}=-4\hat{j}+3\widehat{k}$

Projection of $\vec{b}-2\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b}+\vec{a}$ is $=\frac{\left (\vec{b}-2\vec{a}\right ).\left (\vec{b}+\vec{a}\right )}{\left |\vec{b}+\vec{a}\right |}$

$=\frac{28+18}{5}=\frac{46}{5}$

text: Let $S$ be the sample space of all five digit numbers. If $p$ is the probability that a randomly selected number from $S$, is a multiple of 7 but not divisible by 5 , then $9p$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Among the 5 digit numbers,

First number divisible by 7 is 10003 and last is 99995.

$\Rightarrow$ Number of numbers divisible by 7.

$=\frac{99995-10003}{7}+1$

$=12857$

First number divisible by 35 is 10010 and last is 99995.

$\Rightarrow$ Number of numbers divisible by 35

$=\frac{99995-10010}{35}+1$

$=2572$

Hence number of numbers divisible by 7 but not by 5

$=12857-2572$

$=10285$

$9p=\frac{10285}{90000}\times 9$

$=1.0285$

text:
Let a function $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ be defined as :

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \int\limits _{0}^{x}(5-|t-3|)dt, & x>4 \\ x^{2}+bx & ,x\leq 4 \end{array} \right.$

where $\mathrm{b}\in \mathrm{ℝ}$. If $f$ is continuous at $x=4$, then which of the following statements is NOT true?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ f(x) is continuous at x = 4

$\Rightarrow f(4^{-})=f(4^{+})$

$\Rightarrow 16+4b=\int\limits _{0}^{4}(5-|t-3|)dt$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{3}(2+t)dt+\int\limits _{3}^{4}(8-t)dt$

$\left.  \left. =2t+\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right )_{0}^{3}+8t-\frac{t^{2}}{3}\right ]_{3}^{4}$

$=6+\frac{9}{2}-0+(32-8)-\left (24-\frac{9}{2}\right )$

$16+4b=15$

$\Rightarrow b=\frac{-1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \int\limits _{0}^{x}5-|t-3|dt & x>4 \\ x^{2}-\frac{x}{4} & x\leq 4 \end{array} \right.$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} 5-|x-3| & x>4 \\ 2x-\frac{1}{4} & x\leq 4 \end{array} \right.$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} 8-x & x>4 \\ 2x-\frac{1}{4} & x\leq 4 \end{array} \right.$

$f^{'}(x)<0=x\in \left (-\infty ,\frac{1}{8}\right )\cup (8,\infty )$

$f^{'}(3)+f^{'}(5)=6-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{35}{4}$

$f^{'}(x)=0\Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{8}$ have local minima

$\therefore$ (C) is only incorrect option.

text: For $k\in \mathrm{ℝ}$, let the solutions of the equation $\cos \left (\sin ^{-1}\left (x\cot \left (\tan ^{-1}\left (\cos \left (\sin ^{-1}x\right )\right )\right )\right )\right )=k,0<|x|<\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ be $α$ and $β$, where the inverse trigonometric functions take only principal values. If the solutions of the equation $x^{2}-bx-5=0$ are $\frac{1}{α^{2}}+\frac{1}{β^{2}}$ and $\frac{α}{β}$, then $\frac{b}{k^{2}}$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $0<|x|<\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, $\cos (\sin ^{-1}x)=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}>0$, and $\cot (\tan ^{-1}u)=\dfrac{1}{u}$ for $u>0$, so

$x\cot \left (\tan ^{-1}\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right )=\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}.$

Since $x^{2}<\dfrac{1}{2}$, $\left |\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\right |<1$, and $\cos (\sin ^{-1}y)=\sqrt{1-y^{2}}$ gives

$k=\sqrt{1-\frac{x^{2}}{1-x^{2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{1-2x^{2}}{1-x^{2}}}.$

Squaring, $k^{2}(1-x^{2})=1-2x^{2}\Rightarrow x^{2}=\dfrac{1-k^{2}}{2-k^{2}}$, so the two solutions are $α=-β$ with $α^{2}=β^{2}=\dfrac{1-k^{2}}{2-k^{2}}$.

Therefore $\dfrac{1}{α^{2}}+\dfrac{1}{β^{2}}=\dfrac{2(2-k^{2})}{1-k^{2}}$ and $\dfrac{α}{β}=-1$.

These are the roots of $x^{2}-bx-5=0$, so their product is $-5$:

$-\frac{2(2-k^{2})}{1-k^{2}}=-5\Rightarrow 4-2k^{2}=5-5k^{2}\Rightarrow k^{2}=\frac{1}{3}.$

Then $\dfrac{1}{α^{2}}+\dfrac{1}{β^{2}}=5$, and $b$ is the sum of the roots: $b=5+(-1)=4$.

$\frac{b}{k^{2}}=\frac{4}{1/3}=12$

Hence, the answer is 12.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: The mean and variance of 10 observations were calculated as 15 and 15 respectively by a student who took by mistake 25 instead of 15 for one observation. Then, the correct standard deviation is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $\frac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}x_{i}}{10}=15$ ..... (1)

$\Rightarrow \sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}x_{i}=150$

and $\frac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}x_{i}^{2}}{10}-15^{2}=15$

$\Rightarrow \sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}x_{i}^{2}=2400$

Replacing 25 by 15 we get

$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{9}x_{i}+25=150$

$\Rightarrow \sum\limits _{i=1}^{9}x_{i}=125$

$\therefore$ Correct mean $=\frac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{9}x_{i}+15}{10}=\frac{125+15}{10}=14$

Similarly, $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{2}x_{i}^{2}=2400-25^{2}=1775$

$\therefore$ Correct variance $=\frac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{9}x_{i}^{2}+15^{2}}{10}-14^{2}$

$=\frac{1775+225}{10}-14^{2}=4$

$\therefore$ Correct $S.D=\sqrt{4}=2$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: An ellipse $E:\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ passes through the vertices of the hyperbola  $H:\frac{x^{2}}{49}-\frac{y^{2}}{64}=-1$. Let the major and minor axes of the ellipse $E$ coincide with the transverse and conjugate axes of the hyperbola $H$, respectively. Let the product of the eccentricities of $E$ and $H$ be $\frac{1}{2}$. If $l$ is the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse $E$, then the value of $113l$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Vertices of hyperbola $=(0,\pm 8)$

As ellipse pass through it i.e.,

$0+\frac{64}{b^{2}}=1\Rightarrow b^{2}=64$ ...... (1)

As major axis of ellipse coincide with transverse axis of hyperbola we have b > a i.e.

$e_{E}=\sqrt{1-\frac{a^{2}}{64}}=\frac{\sqrt{64-a^{2}}}{8}$

and $e_{H}=\sqrt{1+\frac{49}{64}}=\frac{\sqrt{113}}{8}$

$\therefore$ $e_{E}\quad .e_{H}=\frac{1}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{64-a^{2}}\sqrt{113}}{64}$

$\Rightarrow (64-a^{2})(113)=32^{2}$

$\Rightarrow a^{2}=64-\frac{1024}{113}$

L.R of ellipse $=\frac{2a^{2}}{b}=\frac{2}{8}\left (\frac{113\times 64-1024}{113}\right )$

$=l=\frac{1552}{113}$

$\therefore$ $113l=1552$

text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation

$\sin \left (2x^{2}\right )\log _{e}\left (\tan x^{2}\right )dy+\left (4xy-4\sqrt{2}x\sin \left (x^{2}-\frac{π}{4}\right )\right )dx=0$, $0<x<\sqrt{\frac{π}{2}}$, which passes through the point $\left (\sqrt{\frac{π}{6}},1\right )$. Then $\left |y\left (\sqrt{\frac{π}{3}}\right )\right |$ is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}+y\left (\frac{4x}{\sin (2x^{2})\ln (\tan x^{2})}\right )=\frac{4\sqrt{2}x\sin \left (x^{2}-\frac{π}{4}\right )}{\sin (2x^{2})\ln (\tan x^{2})}$

$I.F=e^{\int \frac{4x}{\sin (2x2)\ln (\tan x2)}dx}$

$=e^{\ln |\ln (\tan x^{2})}=\ln (\tan x^{2})$

$\therefore$ $\int d(y.\ln (\tan x^{2}))=\int \frac{4\sqrt{2}x\sin \left (x^{2}-\frac{π}{4}\right )}{\sin (2x^{2})}dx$

$\Rightarrow y\ln (\tan x^{2})=\ln \left |\frac{\sec x^{2}+\tan x^{2}}{\mathrm{cosec}x^{2}-\cot x^{2}}\right |+C$

$\ln \left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )=\ln \left (\frac{\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}}{2-\sqrt{3}}\right )+C$

$e=\ln \left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )-\ln \left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2-\sqrt{3}}\right )$

For $y\left (\sqrt{\frac{π}{3}}\right )$

$y\ln \left (\sqrt{3}\right )=\ln \left |\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}\right |+\ln \left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )-\ln \left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}}\right )$

$=\ln \left (2+\sqrt{3}\right )+\ln \left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )+\ln \left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )-\ln \left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2-\sqrt{3}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow y\ln \sqrt{3}=\ln \left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{y}{2}\ln 3=-\frac{1}{2}\ln 3$

$\Rightarrow y=1$

$\therefore$ $\left |y\left (\sqrt{\frac{π}{3}}\right )\right |=1$.

text: Let $f(x)=2x^{2}-x-1$ and $\mathrm{S}=\{n\in \mathrm{ℤ}:|f(n)|\leq 800\}$. Then, the value of $\sum\limits _{n\in S}f(n)$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ $|f(n)|\leq 800$

$\Rightarrow -800\leq 2n^{2}-n-1\leq 800$

$\Rightarrow 2n^{2}-n-801\leq 0$

$\therefore$ $n\in \left [\frac{-\sqrt{6409}+1}{4},\frac{\sqrt{6409}+1}{4}\right ]$ and $n\in z$

$\therefore$ $n=-19,-18,-17,..........,19,20.$

$\therefore$ $\sum \left (2n^{2}-n-1\right )=2\sum n^{2}-\sum n-\sum 1$.

$=2.\qquad 2.\left (1^{2}+2^{2}+...+19^{2}\right )+2.20^{2}-20-40$

$=10620$

text: Let $S$ be the set containing all $3\times 3$ matrices with entries from $\{-1,0,1\}$. The total number of matrices $A\in S$ such that the sum of all the diagonal elements of $A^{\mathrm{T}}A$ is 6 is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Sum of all diagonal elements is equal to sum of square of each element of the matrix.

i.e., $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} a_{1} & a_{2} & a_{3} \\ b_{1} & b_{2} & b_{3} \\ c_{1} & c_{2} & c_{3} \end{array}\right ]$

then $t_{r}(A\qquad .A^{T})$

$=a_{1}^{2}+a_{2}^{2}+a_{3}^{2}+b_{1}^{2}+b_{2}^{2}+b_{3}^{2}+c_{1}^{2}+c_{2}^{2}+c_{3}^{2}$

$\because$ $a_{i},b_{i},c_{i}\in \{-1,0,1\}$ for $i=1,2,3$

$\therefore$ Exactly three of them are zero and rest are 1 or $-$1.

Total number of possible matrices ${}^{9}C_{3}\times 2^{6}$

$=\frac{9\times 8\times 7}{6}\times 64$

$=5376$

text: If the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse $x^{2}+4y^{2}+2x+8y-λ=0$ is 4 , and $l$ is the length of its major axis, then $λ+l$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Equation of ellipse is : $x^{2}+4y^{2}+2x+8y-λ=0$

$(x+1)^{2}+4(y+1)^{2}=λ+5$

$\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{λ+5}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{\left (\frac{λ+5}{4}\right )}=1$

Length of latus rectum $=\frac{2.\left (\frac{λ+5}{4}\right )}{\sqrt{λ+5}}=4$.

$\therefore$ $λ=59$.

Length of major axis $=2.\qquad \sqrt{λ+5}=16=l$

$\therefore$ $λ+l=75$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: Let $S=\left \{z\in \mathrm{ℂ}:z^{2}+\bar{z}=0\right \}$. Then $\sum\limits _{z\in S}(\mathrm{Re}(z)+\mathrm{Im}(z))$ is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ $z^{2}+z–=0$

Let $z=x+iy$

$\therefore$ $x^{2}-y^{2}+2ixy+x-iy=0$

$(x^{2}-y^{2}+x)+i(2xy-y)=0$

$\therefore$ $x^{2}-y^{2}+x=0$ and $(2x-1)y=0$

if $x=+\frac{1}{2}$ then $y=\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

And if $y=0$ then $x=0,-1$

$\therefore$ $z=0+0i,-1+0i,\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i,\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$

$\therefore$ $\sum (R_{e}(z)+I_{m}(z))=0$
